title: The Surprising Power of Atomic Habits
coreMove: Treat invisible progress as banked rather than absent, and keep acting on the days the graph looks flat

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school orchestra teacher tracking a second-violin section that has not improved at concerts for eight weeks
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher in her fourth year who is privately considering reseating the section
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she abandons a rehearsal protocol that is actually working three weeks before it would have shown
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the teacher names what she has banked — intonation drills logged, scale tempos crept up by a metronome click — and decides to keep the protocol for the spring concert

exampleSpecs.domain: a line cook saving fifteen seconds per plate on a six-top pasta station
exampleSpecs.audience: a line cook two years out of culinary school working a 180-cover Saturday
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether shaving seconds off mise en place compounds into surviving the rush without the expo screaming
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the cook does the math out loud over a prep table — fifteen seconds times forty plates times five nights — and sees the hour he has been quietly buying back

exampleSpecs.domain: a couple six months into paying down twenty-eight thousand dollars of credit card debt
exampleSpecs.audience: a married couple in their early thirties who feel like the balance has barely moved
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether one of them cashes out a small index fund to feel progress, breaking the plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: one partner pulls up the amortization curve and points to where the principal line steepens in month fourteen, and they agree to keep the autopay

exampleSpecs.domain: a physical therapist coaching a stroke patient through week eleven of grip-strength exercises
exampleSpecs.audience: a PT working in an outpatient clinic with a patient ready to quit
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the patient stops three weeks before the dynamometer would have moved
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the PT shows the patient her own session notes, where range of motion has crept by two degrees a week, and reframes the flat number on the squeeze gauge as the last thing to change rather than the only thing that matters

exampleSpecs.domain: imagine an ice cube sitting in a room you are slowly warming one degree at a time, from twenty-five degrees up
exampleSpecs.audience: any reader who has ever quit a habit at week six
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the reader sees the difference between thirty-one degrees and thirty-two as the difference between nothing happening and everything happening
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the temperature crosses thirty-two and the cube melts, and the reader is asked which of the previous seven degrees did the work

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional sales manager reviewing a junior rep who has made eighty cold calls a day for two months with three meetings booked
exampleSpecs.audience: a manager about to write a performance improvement plan
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a rep who is actually building the right habit gets cut the week before her pipeline turns
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager looks back from month five, sees the meetings booked curve bend upward in week ten, and recognizes the call-quality notes she had dismissed as the leading indicator she should have trusted
